🇮🇱🇮🇷🇹🇷 Former Israeli intelligence officer: Netanyahu wants ANOTHER IRAN WAR, and TURKEY could be next

Brandon caught up with Shaiel Ben-Ephraim, a former officer in Israel's elite Unit 8200 who has become one of the country's most outspoken critics.

And he made a rather extraordinary prediction.

He believes another U.S.-Israeli confrontation with Iran is virtually certain after the November 3 midterms.

But here's where it gets interesting.

Shaiel thinks Washington and Netanyahu want VERY different things.

Trump may be looking for a quick military operation. Netanyahu, he argues, wants a much larger campaign aimed at regime change, one that could also strengthen his hand in Israel's ongoing coalition negotiations.

And Iran might not be the end of it.

Shaiel says Israeli political and military circles are increasingly treating TURKEY as their next major strategic rival, particularly in Syria.

Turkey is a NATO member with a formidable military. Yet Shaiel believes some Israeli hardliners would welcome a prolonged confrontation, even if it begins through proxies rather than direct fighting.

We also discussed disturbing footage from Tel Aviv, where a pro-Netanyahu demonstrator invoked Nazi death camps against Israeli left-wing protesters.

Shaiel sees it as evidence of something deeply troubling inside Israeli politics.

But he argues the country's biggest internal divide isn't actually over Palestine. It's over religion, military service and the growing resentment between secular Israelis and the ultra-Orthodox.

His longer-term concern is that the educated, economically productive Israelis sustaining the country's military and technological advantages are increasingly leaving.

The question we kept coming back to was whether Israel's leadership has any political incentive to end these confrontations.

Shaiel's assessment was unsettling: Netanyahu may benefit more from keeping the country on a permanent war footing than from securing a lasting peace.

If you watch it with the audio synced to the public flight data, she says that when they hit 10,000 feet. She says "we're out of ten" which is a common pilot term. She's saying they just blew through ten thousand, which at their rate of descent is critically low.

She was relaying to ATC her ever increasing rate of descent, even her angle of bank. She knew exactly what her altitude was.

The last report she gave was that she was descending at over 20,000 feet/minute.

Process that: nearly 4 miles a minute straight down. She was hyper aware of her orientation, descent rate, etc.

They were decending into a thunderstorm. Violent winds caused them to go into a high speed stall while in a 60 degree bank which caused an overspeed condition where essentially they started moving so fast that their control surfaces were useless.

There is absolutely no wreckage around that crater. Everything was obliterated. Brutal.

They are all screaming and yelling how they;re going to die and they are out of time, then complete silence.

We all fear our mortality. I would rather go out instantaneously over a drawn out disease or something that forces you to recognize your death for days and days.

These poor souls were petrified for seconds. Not days like cancer or something along those lines.

A full minute to see death rushing towards you knowing there was nothing you can do to stop it. Thinking about all the things you'll never be able to do, loved ones you'll never be able to hold again, regrets you can never fix. All with simultaneous, overwhelming, absolute terror. The moment of death may have been quick, but the rest of it was not quick at all.

Not only that but trying to also think critically to try and save your life, trying to dig deep into your training. Panicking even more. Then realizing it’s getting to where it’s too late. More panic. Boom. Sad to think about.
